core_obligations: Recall that R is a G-ring exactly when every local ring has geometrically regular formal fibres (proof lines 12204-12205).

For primes q inside p, identify the algebra R at p completed, tensor over R with the residue field of q, with the algebra (R/q) at p completed, tensor over R/q with the same residue field, which is the display in the proof (proof lines 12205-12209).
Conclude that the two conditions of the statement test the same family of algebras over the same residue fields, so the equivalence follows (proof lines 12209-12211).

The nearest public records are 348 (12429-12491, tag 07QR, henselization preserves the G-ring property) and 1799 (12355-12389, tag 07PS); both are statements of the same G-ring block that begin after this card's interval ends, and public 348 proves a different result about henselization.
difficulty_reason: The lemma reformulates the G-ring condition for a Noetherian ring: instead of asking that every local ring have geometrically regular formal fibres, it is enough to check, for every pair of primes q inside p, that the algebra (R/q) at p completed, tensor over R/q with the residue field of q, is geometrically regular over that field (statement lines 12193-12201). The proof is eight lines (proof lines 12204-12211) and consists of the displayed identification of the two algebras over the residue field of q, together with the sentence that the result follows from it. The content is the base change computation: completing R at p and then reducing modulo q gives the same algebra as first dividing by q and then completing at the image prime, and the tensor factor over the residue field is the same on both sides, so testing one family of algebras is testing the other. The author leaves the identification itself to the reader; the surrounding discussion of the chapter is what fixes the meaning of G-ring and of geometric regularity used here.
